title: Endpoint pointwise convergence for the Schrodinger equation in higher dimensions

issues.description: Not a demonstrated error, only a limit on what I checked. The whole lossless weak estimate depends on two things: the new frame theorem, whose proof is about 1800 lines, and the transverse saving. The transverse saving imports the 'limiting information calculus' from the planar companion PSE2026 (Sec. 3). I did not verify either one line by line. The sibling report on the planar companion (rank 47) has the same gap in its coverage. The higher-dimensional extension of those companion lemmas is asserted to hold 'with the hypotheses stated at their points of use'. I did not independently confirm that this extension is valid.
issues.evidence: 'The proof uses the limiting information calculus of [PSE2026, Section 3] ... We state the usable facts below and prove the changes needed in dimension n.'

coverage:
I read the introduction, weak.tex, angular.tex and sparse.tex in full. I also read endpoint.tex Secs 9.1 to 9.2 (the compact-layer reduction, the lossless short-time weak estimate, the dual square sum with the time tree, and the L^1 maximal theorem), the input part of fractal.tex (the Du-Zhang input, the weighted fractal estimate and Fourier layers), the opening of transverse.tex (multilinear estimates with polynomial dependence and the pruned incident-tube model), the frame theorem statement, and the tuple bound and induction completion in flattening.tex.

I checked these by hand:
- Rescaling exponent: N^{n/2}L^{-e} = N^s.
- Time-tree bounds d_j(J) <= m^{2-2/p}, d_j(J) <= r^{2s} m, the geometric mean, the heavy-path weighted Cauchy-Schwarz and the convexity-deficit telescoping.
- Chebyshev step in the large-D range of the weak theorem, giving the exponent chi^zeta L^{2n}.
- In the sparse estimate: the transport cancellation K^{2-(n+2)beta} = K^{-beta}, the cancellation beta - a_n - theta_n = 0, the terminal power of l, and the broad-gain saturation inequalities.
- The Du-Zhang Thm 1.6 exponents, including a sanity check that the case alpha = n+1 gives the trivial bound R^{1/2}.
- Incident weight w >= L^{-e} and Kakeya saturation in the tube model.
- Angular induction exponent Gamma, with Gamma(2,0) = beta - b, and the exact cancellation of chi^{2a}.
- Frame-to-tuple algebra after raising to the power k/(k+2) = 1 - beta.
- Final scale cancellation and the margin n - 1/2 - e = (n-1)/(2(n+1)).

I also tested the frame bound |Y| <= H_g^{-2} sum D_i/A_i^2 heuristically on a single-focus example and on a Talbot-lattice example. Both saturate it exactly and neither violates it.

Not verified: the proof of the frame theorem (the rest of frame.tex), packets.tex (buffered refined decoupling and related results), most of transverse.tex, and wall.tex.
main_claim: For n >= 3 and f in H^{n/(2(n+1))}(R^n), the Gaussian-regularized Schrodinger evolution converges, uniformly in 0 < t < 1, on one full-measure set to a time-continuous representative v with v(x,0) = f*(x). The proof goes through a local L^1 maximal bound with no endpoint loss. That bound comes from a weak-L^p (p > 2) short-time estimate at exactly N^s, combined with a common dyadic time tree.
sibling_notes: Family 080 had one sibling on the board: the planar companion (rank 47), reported as no_gap_found. It checked the Sec 9 time tree and convexity deficit; I checked the n-dimensional version of the same mechanism here and it also holds. The sibling noted the same unverified dependence on the transverse and frame arguments, and I record that overlap as the remaining risk.
